title: MCoE G6 IT Services
description: This is a non-personal service contract providing a broad range of services, encompassing system administration, help desk support, hardware/software installation, and troubleshooting. The contractor is responsible for administration, management, parts, supplies, tools and equipment and accountability of GFE systems used in support of programs of instruction (POI). The contractor shall provide technically qualified personnel with strong English language skills requiring direct interaction with users and technical documentation. There will be a one-month phase-in to avoid any service disruptions and to mitigate any lag time in performance of work to facilitate on-boarding of personnel. This includes obtaining Common Access Cards (CAC), all accounts required for access to NIPR resources and Information Assurance training, all prerequisites for providing support. Additional allowances may be flexed to meet manpower or service(s) requirements that can possibly occur later that could include but not limited to additional Tech Support for hardware/software installation, troubleshooting system administration and custom, in accordance with the PWS.

title: RFQ SF330 - NOAA Western Region Architect and Engineering IDIQ
description: 1. GENERAL INFORMATION The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Corporate Services and Acquisition Division (CSAD), Facilities Engineering Office � Western Region (FEO-WR) is soliciting Standard Form 330 (SF330) packages from qualified Architect-Engineer (A/E) firms. This procurement is being conducted in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 36.2 with The Brooks Act (40 U.S.C. 1101 et seq). IDIQ Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Total Capacity: The total shared capacity of the Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) shall not exceed $9.9M to be allocated among successful offerors over the life of the contract. Guaranteed Minimum: A minimum of $2,500 in task order work shall be awarded under the contract. Period of Performance: Five (5) year ordering period. Individual requirements will be executed via Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task orders. 2. SCOPE OF SERVICES The purpose of the contract is to obtain professional multi-discipline architectural, engineering, and construction management services for repair, renovation, alteration, new construction and expansion across DOC/NOAA facilities, with design excellence and adherence to sound design practices, resulting in projects that meet NOAA�s requirements and are delivered in a cost effective and efficient manner. The A-E shall furnish all necessary personnel, equipment, materials, and services to perform individual firm-fixed-price task orders as required. Typical A/E services include the following: project management, master and strategic planning, facility programming, facility condition assessments (FCA), geotechnical and soil investigations, land surveying (topographic, boundary, and utility), cost estimating, value engineering, engineering studies and analyses, architectural and engineering design services (including design-build and traditional design-bid-build), interior design, furniture design and procurement, seismic studies, coastal engineering, environmental assessments and industrial hygiene, historic preservation and archaeological surveys, commissioning/re-commissioning/retro-commissioning, construction management, construction administration, quality assurance, construction inspection services, life-cycle cost analysis, peer reviews, claims consultation, security and acoustical studies, and post-occupancy evaluations. Typical projects include Design and construction support for new facilities as well as the renovation, repair, expansion, and demolition of existing facilities. Services encompass seismic design and structural retrofits; fire-life safety design in accordance with NFPA and applicable codes; comprehensive facility condition assessments and existing condition reporting; and pre-design site investigations, including utility analysis. Scope includes the repair, alteration, improvement, and remodeling of building exteriors, interior spaces, and building systems�such as mechanical, plumbing, electrical, structural, fire protection, roofing, elevator/escalator systems, and specialized seawater systems. Work extends to the preservation and renovation of historic structures, as well as the repair and new construction of coastal and marine infrastructure, including piers, jetties, wharves, and seawalls. Typical facilities include Office buildings, Warehouses and storage buildings, Laboratories and research facilities, Wharf and pier structures/infrastructure, Seawalls and other coastal construction, Communications installations, Weather forecast offices, Data centers, and Communication/data equipment installations/platforms. 3. GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE While the Government reserves the right to utilize the contractor in other U.S. locations on an exception basis, the primary geographic areas are defined as follows: Western Region Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oregon, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, Washington, Wyoming, American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, and the Federated States of Micronesia. 4. CONSIDERATION To be considered under this Request for Qualifications, firms must demonstrate the capability of providing the following minimum requirements: 1) Architectural, civil/structural, geotechnical, seismic design engineering, mechanical, electrical, marine, fire-life safety engineering, and LEED design in conformance to each project jurisdiction; 2) Demonstrated capability of key personnel to respond promptly and effectively to unforeseen emergencies within the primary project locations; 5. EVALUATION CRITERIA The Government plans to award up to three (3) separate A-E Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts to comprise one (1) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for professional A-E services from this announcement. Each respondent�s SF 330 submittal package will be evaluated in accordance with RFO 36.202 procedures. The selection criteria, in descending order of importance will be as follows: 1. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence 2. Professional Qualifications 3. Past Performance The Government will select at least three of the most highly qualified firms for interviews. The Government will evaluate offerors based on the following factors, listed in descending order of importance. The Government will conduct a comprehensive assessment of each offeror�s submission and relevant qualifications to determine the most highly-qualified firms. Factor 1: Specialized Experience and Technical Competence Offerors will be evaluated on the relevancy, breadth, and diversity of their specialized experience as detailed in SF 330, Part 1, Sections F, G, and H, specifically considering projects from the past five (5) years in terms of type, size, and complexity. Demonstrated expertise in Design-Build (specifically RFP development), Construction Administration, and commitment to sustainable energy/design (LEED/Green Globes) is critical. Respondents must provide five (5) recent and relevant projects; any project provided in addition to the five will not be considered. Submissions missing any of the following requested information may be assessed a deficiency: Contract/Task Order Number Project Title Location Prime Firm with % of self-performed work Start and Completion dates If the project is not yet complete, identify the current phase/stage of the project. Fully completed projects will carry more weight than projects still in design Description of the project in sufficient detail and clearly document how it is relevant to the scope of this project Factor 2: Professional Qualifications Offerors will be evaluated on the professional qualifications of key personnel from the primary firm and proposed consultants, as evidenced by SF 330, Part 1, Section E. Evaluation will prioritize professional registration; education, training, and relevant experience; tenure with the firm; and specialized certifications (e.g., DBIA, CEP, NEBB/BCA for CxA). Offerors will be evaluated on the firm�s capacity to manage large, multi-disciplined, complex design efforts and execute multiple concurrent task orders across the diverse Western Region. The Government will assess the adequacy of in-house disciplines, the strength of established consulting partners, and the quality of proposed plans for staff augmentation and project response. Factor 3: Past Performance Offerors will be evaluated on their past performance history on recent and relevant contracts for A-E services with Government agencies and private industry. Evaluations will assess the quality of work, cost control, general management, cooperativeness, compliance with performance schedules, and any record of significant claims against the firm due to improper or incomplete A/E services. The Government will evaluate past performance using submitted SF 330s, CPARS, independent references, and information regarding predecessor companies, key personnel, or major subcontractors. title: France – Construction work for warehouses and industrial buildings – Conception et réalisation d'une plateforme logistique sur un foncier de 12 000m² ( minimum), par construction neuve ou réhabilitation d'un bâtiment existant sur le secteur de Mareuil Les Meaux ou Nanteuil Les Meaux (77Seine et Marne) sous format d'une Prise à bail en l'état futur d'achèvement (BEFA)
description: Conception et réalisation d'une Plateforme Logistique avec terrain ou réhabilitation d’un bâtiment existant avec une surface de 4 000m² ( dont 578 m²) sur un foncier de 12 000 m² ( minimum) dans une zone géographique située sur le secteur de Mareuil Les Meaux ou Nanteuil Les Meaux (77-Seine et Marne), avec voirie autorisée aux poids lourds. Le Projet souhaité est sous forme de BEFA. Les candidats pourront également proposer toute solution alternative pertinente, notamment une VEFA. L'acceptation et les modalités d'examen de ces solutions seront précisées dans les documents de la consultation en phase offre. La Maitrise d’Ouvrage est ouverte à toute solution alternative pouvant répondre aux exigences de ce besoin fonctionnel, toutefois toute candidature hors du périmètre mentionné sera déclarée irrecevable. Le terrain ou bâti proposé devra avoir une contenance suffisante pour répondre aux exigences du projet (Surface de bâtiment, nombre de places de parking et allées de circulation associées, nombre de quais Poids lourds/Véhicules légers y compris aires de retournement associées). Les ratios habituels sont de 1m² bâtis pour 3m² de foncier minimum, selon configuration de la parcelle.

title: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Mission Training Complex (MTC)
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This synopsis is hereby issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203, to announce the Government's intent to award a 8-month, Firm Fixed-Price Bridge Contract, on a noncompetitive basis to Trideum Corporation (CAGE 351S9) for the Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Mission Training Complex Capabilities Support (MTCCS) effort. This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract under statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(l) set forth in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Procedures, Guidance, and Information 206-302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Army Contracting Command-Orlando (ACC-ORL} and JBSA have identified a need to award a sole source contract to Trideum Corp (CAGE 351S9), to continue performance of JBSA MTCCS requirements. The current JBSA MTCCS Task Order expires 28 JAN 26. The contemplated sole source contract will include a limited performance period of five (5) months, commencing 29 JAN 2026 - 30 SEP 2026, ensuring continuation of mission command (MC) training at the JBSA Mission Training Complexes (MTCs). Services performed under this sole source contract will include the continuation of non-personal services to support the Mission Training Complex (MTC) to units stationed at and supported by Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA). No other contractor is in the position to assemble a large team of administrative, program management and subject matter experts (SMEs) who specialize in providing individual through collective Mission Command (MC} training, by the expiration of the current JBSA MTCCS contract performance period (28 JAN 26}. Award to anyone other than the incumbent contractor (Trideum) would result in a significant break in service. Award of this limited Bridge Contract is result of decrements identified in the Program Objective Memorandum for Fiscal Years FY27 through FY31 (POM 27-31), and as a result, the JBSA MTC will close at the end of FY26. This is NOT a request for competitive quotes. The Government intends to negotiate solely under statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 2304(c}(l) set forth in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1. Any interested firms must identity their interest and capability to respond to the requirement no later than 15 business days after this notice posts. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Please respond by 24 DEC 2025 at 1300 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST). Your response must include your stated technical knowledge of and experience with mission command (MC) training and information to demonstrate the Contractor's ability to complete Phase-In activities and commence full performance by the end of the current JBSA contract (28 JAN 2026). Send your response to Will Bass via willie.c.bass2.civ@army.mil. All responding contractors must be registered to the System for Award Management (SAM).

title: TECHNOLOGY/BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: Laser-induced Propulsion of Micro-scaled Projectiles for ICF Target Manufacture
description: Opportunity: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), operated by the Lawrence Livermore National Security (LLNS), LLC under contract no. DE-AC52-07NA27344 (Contract 44) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is offering the opportunity to enter into a collaboration to further develop and commercialize its diamond target filling and capping technology. Background: Inertial confinement fusion targets can be challenging to fill and cap in their sensitive manufacturing environments, often requiring days to fill and cap in a highly manual and time intensive manner. Description: This method propels micro-scaled projectiles with controlled momentum transfer using femtosecond laser ablation. By ablation of material from the backside, micro-scaled objects or projectiles can be accelerated to controlled velocities depending on the impinging laser energy and the projectile mass. The efficiency of the momentum transfer can be greatly enhanced by using non- thermal ablation using ultra short laser technology. This method can be applied for directed ejection of prefabricated plugs for ICF diamond capsules without mechanical contact. Additionally, the inserted plug can be pressurized and further pressed inside the capsule hole causing diamond material fusion. Advantages/Benefits: Enables rapid capsule fueling and capping on the order of minutes in scalable manner Lowers time and other OPEX costs for high volume manufacturing of ICF targets. Potential Applications: Inertial confinement fusion and target manufacturing. Other benefits of this method could be medical and biological application for controlled injection of micro-scaled objects. Development Status: Current stage of technology development: TRL ? 0-2 ? 3-5 ? 5-9 LLNL has filed for patent protection on this invention. LLNL is seeking industry partners with a demonstrated ability to bring such inventions to the market. Moving critical technology beyond the Laboratory to the commercial world helps our licensees gain a competitive edge in the marketplace. All licensing activities are conducted under policies relating to the strict nondisclosure of company proprietary information. Please visit the IPO website at https://ipo.llnl.gov/resources for more information on working with LLNL and the industrial partnering and technology transfer process. title: TECHNOLOGY/BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: Development of a High-Capacity, Acid-Stable Lanmodulin Immobilization Platform for REE Separation
description: Opportunity: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), operated by the Lawrence Livermore National Security (LLNS), LLC under contract no. DE-AC52-07NA27344 (Contract 44) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is offering the opportunity to enter into a collaboration to further develop and commercialize its development of a High-Capacity, Acid-Stable Lanmodulin Immobilization Platform for REE Separation. Background: Rare earth elements (REEs) are critically required for high tech as well as defense applications. Therefore, building a resilient domestic supply chain for REEs is a national security imperative. Lanmodulin (LanM), a bacterial protein, and its variants immobilized on a column provide a biotechnology approach for REE extraction as they have a very high specificity and affinity for REEs. However, LanM requires stability at ultra-low pH (typically below 3.0 and often down to 1.5), high metal concentrations, and elevated flow rates, posing unique challenges for support materials and immobilization chemistry. Description: After extensive screening of commercial ion-exchange resins and immobilization methods, a proprietary resin was identified as uniquely capable of supporting high-density LanM immobilization while preserving REE selectivity and operational durability. The optimized platform demonstrated superior mechanical and chemical stability, with less than 10% capacity loss over 11 weeks at pH 3 and enabled high-resolution separation of REE. The method allowed operation at substantially increased flow rates with minimal loss in separation performance. This approach is generalizable to naturally occurring or engineered LanM variants. Advantages/Benefits: The resin demonstrated superior mechanical and chemical stability, with less than 10% capacity loss over 11 weeks at pH 3 The resin functions at low pH required for REE separation using LanM The resin works at high metal concentrations, and maintains elevated flow rates Potential Applications: This technology enables robust and scalable REE purification under industrially relevant conditions, offering significant advantages over traditional methods in terms of selectivity, throughput, and operational stability The platform also holds promise for broader uses, including the recovery of actinides and lanthanides in nuclear fuel cycle management, environmental remediation of metal-contaminated waters, and the purification of valuable metals from industrial and electronic waste streams. Development Status: Current stage of technology development: TRL ? 0-2 ? 3-5 ? 5-9 LLNL has filed for patent protection on this invention. LLNL is seeking industry partners with a demonstrated ability to bring such inventions to the market. Moving critical technology beyond the Laboratory to the commercial world helps our licensees gain a competitive edge in the marketplace. All licensing activities are conducted under policies relating to the strict nondisclosure of company proprietary information. Please visit the IPO website at https://ipo.llnl.gov/resources for more information on working with LLNL and the industrial partnering and technology transfer process. Note: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT. Companies interested in commercializing LLNL's development of a High-Capacity, Acid-Stable Lanmodulin Immobilization Platform for REE Separation should provide an electronic OR written statement of interest, which includes the following: Company Name and address. The name, address, and telephone number of a point of contact. A description of corporate expertise and/or facilities relevant to commercializing this technology. Please provide a complete electronic OR written statement to ensure consideration of your interest in LLNL's development of a High-Capacity, Acid-Stable Lanmodulin Immobilization Platform for REE Separation. The subject heading in an email response should include the Notice ID and/or the title of LLNL�s Technology/Business Opportunity and directed to the Primary and Secondary Point of Contacts listed below. Written responses should be directed to: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory Innovation and Partnerships Office P.O. Box 808, L-779 Livermore, CA 94551-0808 Attention: 2026-076

description: INDUSTRY DAY: Department of Homeland Security, United States Coast Guard (USCG), Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC), CG Yard Location: USCG Yard, 2401 Hawkins Point Rd, Baltimore MD 21226 Description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an Industry Day event on 08 January 2026 at 9:00am ET. All interested parties are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view the registration information, attachments, and details below. The USCG plans to conduct a multi-phased approach to market research including: 1) requesting submission of capabilities statement, 2) an in-person industry day, and 3) one-on-one engagements with industry. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) will be holding an Industry Day event to engage with industry about the USCG�s needs relating to a potential upcoming requirement(s) and obtain information from industry as the USCG continues to seek a system of work platforms to facilitate exterior hull preservation on the 154� WPC Fast Response Cutter. The USCG will share more information about the scope of the requirements, the challenges we have identified, and the goals of the program. The venue has a capacity limitation; therefore, each vendor is limited to two participants. To participate, vendors should email Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist). All responses are due no later than 26 December 2025 at 4:00pm EST. The in-person Industry Day presentation will be recorded and or transcribed and publicly posted.? This is a follow-on to the USCG�s previously published Request for Information (RFI) that preliminarily describes the USCG�s needs. The previously published RFI (70Z04026RFI62204Y00) is attached to this Special Notice for reference purposes. INDUSTRY DAY AND ONE-ON-ONE SESSIONS GENERAL Industry Day The USCG will host an Industry Day on 08 January 2026, from 9:00am � 11:30am ET. A finalized agenda for the event will be sent out by 02 January 2026. In preparation for the in-person Industry Day, USCG asks interested vendors to review the information provided in the appendices and submit questions to Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist), so the USCG can be prepared to share the questions received and the answers. Please be advised that all questions and answers will be shared publicly. Therefore, interested parties are encouraged not to submit proprietary information with their questions. One-on-One Sessions The one-on-one engagements with vendors will occur immediately following the in-person industry day on 08 January 2026. Vendors should express their interest in a one-on-one session when registering via email. The USCG will follow up, no later than 02 January 2026, with a scheduled time for one-on-one engagements. There will be approximately 8 time slots available for one-on-one sessions. Each appointment is limited to approximately 15 minutes. Your confirmed one-on-one time will be included as a follow-on email to your registration confirmation. The purpose of these one-on-one sessions is to gather objective feedback, foster open dialogue, and obtain information from industry as the USCG continues to seek a system of work platforms to facilitate exterior hull preservation on the 154� WPC Fast Response Cutter. These sessions are not a platform for vendor promotion. title: Sweden – Evaluation consultancy services – Vidareutveckling av verktyg för samskapande kunskaps- och innovationsprocesser
description: UPPDRAGET OCH DESS OMFATTNING Västerbottens regionala utvecklingsstrategi 2020–2030 slår fast att länets utveckling förutsätter fördjupade och gränsöverskridande samarbeten. Visionen är en attraktiv region där olikheter skapar utvecklingskraft. Flera förhållanden begränsar i dag den förmågan: • Arbete organiseras i stuprör, vilket försvårar samverkan mellan lokal, regional, nationell och internationell nivå. • Små och medelstora företag behandlas ofta som en homogen grupp trots att deras behov skiljer sig åt. • Kunskap, relationer och nätverk är i hög grad personberoende och riskerar att gå förlorade när projekt avslutas eller nyckelpersoner slutar. • Lokala initiativ synliggörs inte alltid på regional nivå, vilket minskar möjligheten att ta tillvara erfarenheter och resultat. • Kommunerna har en central roll i den regionala utvecklingen men saknar ofta resurser, kapacitet och tidig delaktighet. • Finansierings- och styrsystem är ofta för tröga för att stödja missionsdriven omställning. • Resultat och metoder från internationella samarbeten, särskilt inom Interreg, integreras inte tillräckligt i de regionala utvecklingsprocesserna. Det finns därmed behov av stärkt förmåga till samverkan och samhandling mellan aktörer, och av strukturer som kopplar samman behov, kunskap och resurser mellan nivåer. Det handlar om funktioner som ger överblick över pågående initiativ, synliggör kopplingar mellan aktörer och möjliggör mer differentierade former av stöd till företag och organisationer. Det handlar också om former för tidig delaktighet, tydligare rollfördelning och ökad förmåga att omsätta resultat från projektverksamheten i konkret regional utveckling, policyutveckling och innovationsprocesser. En stärkt koppling mellan aktörer och nivåer ger bättre förutsättningar att ta tillvara befintlig kunskap, identifiera kompletterande insatser och minska dubbelarbete. Lokala behov kan tydligare relateras till regionala, nationella och europeiska prioriteringar, vilket ökar precisionen i insatser riktade till företag och organisationer. Denna upphandling avser vidareutveckling av verktyg för samskapande kunskaps- och innovationsprocesser. title: MRO - Africa Region
description: This notice shall not be construed as a solicitation announcement. The United States Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this notice. The purpose of this acquisition is to: 1. Ensure uninterrupted management and coordination of Maintenance, Repair, and Operations (MRO) supply chain activities across Africa. 2. Maintain the logistical capacity and capabilities to source, consolidate, and deliver a wide range of commercial items necessary for the maintenance, repair, and operation of facilities. 3. Avoid costly delays and/or disruptions in mission-critical operations by ensuring continued MRO support while a competitive follow-on contract is being awarded. The MRO program is a major component of DLA Troop Support Europe & Africa's logistics capabilities and is an essential and necessary part of fulfilling the Agency's requirements. The prime vendor plays a central role in executing the mission's objectives by maintaining the supplier network, transportation agreements, and systems integration needed to ensure timely delivery of MRO supplies, inform logistical decisions, and fulfill DLA's obligations for customer support. This bridge action is a continuation of services currently being performed under IDIQ: SPE5B1-21-D-0004, awarded to TWI USA, LLC. The follow-on acquisition is already in progress, but due to procurement timelines, a limitedduration extension is necessary to prevent a lapse in mission-essential service. A sole-source bridge is being pursued because any transition of work to a new entity at this stage would introduce unacceptable delays and inefficiencies in fulfilling the Agency's requirements. The incumbent�s business systems, including established supplier and transportation agreements, unique understanding of customer requirements, and systems integration with DLA Troop Support, are deeply embedded in ongoing operations. Restarting or onboarding a new contractor for a short duration would result in duplicative costs, loss of institutional knowledge, and disruption to time-sensitive logistical support. This contract supports the MRO requirements for Africa. The prime vendor serves as the central hub for managing all aspects of the supply chain, including the sourcing of Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) supplies; plumbing supplies; electrical products; various tools; chemical and rubber products; construction supplies (e.g., cement, lumber, bricks); prefabricated structures; appliances; utility vehicles; and perimeter security items, as well as related incidental commercial services. All work is governed by the Statement of Work / Performance Work Statement. The contractor ensures continuity across the supply chain, supports logistical management, and maintains the technical infrastructure needed to support seamless EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) system integration, enabling timely and efficient delivery of MRO supplies to meet DLA's readiness needs. The eighty-nine (89) day bridge contract modification is required to ensure effective continuity of operations from 20 NOV 2026 through 16 FEB 2027.

title: Norway – Internal audit services – Internal Audit Services
description: 1. Purpose and agreement period 1.1 Purpose The contract shall ensure NTNU access to independent, objective and risk based internal audit services of high professional quality. The internal audit shall contribute to strengthen NTNU ́s performance management, risk management and internal control and give the board an independent basis for assessment and follow-up. The agreement shall facilitate for continuity, good business understanding and a long-term cooperation, at the same time that the audit work shall be able to be adapted to changes in NTNU ́s risk picture, business and priorities. 2. Content of the Service 2.1 General The tenderer shall provide an overall internal audit service that includes: Preparation of annual risk based audit plan. Implementation of internal audits within the approved audit plan. Reporting audit results, findings and recommendations. Follow-up of measures after completed audits. Consultancy services for performance management, risk management and internal control within the limits of the independence of the internal audit. Ongoing dialogue with relevant parts of NTNU's management and organisation. Reporting to the board and other relevant decision-making bodies. Tenderers shall carry out the assignments with due diligence, objectivity and quality, in accordance with Global Standards for Internal Audit (GIAS) set by The Institute of Internal Auditors, in the at any given time applicable version, and NTNU ́s instructions for internal audits. If an assignment cannot be carried out in accordance with GIAS, the tenderer shall provide information on this in the report, stating which standards have not been followed, the reason and consequences for observations and conclusions. Special audits or surveys shall be possible if there is a need that is not included in the annual audit plan. 2.2 NTNU ́s guidelines The guidelines are attached. The version of the instructions that apply when the contract is signed, is dated 29 April 2018. October 2020. NTNU can update the guidelines during the agreement period. Changes that do not significantly affect the tenderer's obligations shall be followed within the agreed remuneration. 2.3 Annual risk assessment and audit plan Tenderers shall annually carry out a general risk assessment of NTNU ́s activities and prepare a justified proposal for the audit plan with the hourly budget for the coming years. The risk assessment shall be based on the understanding of NTNU's social mission, organisation, strategic aims and framework conditions. Tenderers shall obtain and assess relevant information from i.a. the board, university management, risk assessments, previous audits and other relevant sources. The tenderer shall justify the priorities. It shall be clear what risks the audits are meant to highlight, and what significant risks are not prioritised and why. The audit plan shall be processed and approved by NTNU's board of directors in accordance with the current management scheme. 2.4 Implementation of audits Each audit shall be planned and carried out based on an approved audit plan. After each audit, the tenderer shall prepare a report that is clear and relevant for decision making. Finds and recommendations shall be prioritised in accordance with materiality and risk. The principal shall continuously receive audit reports from the individual audits. The results of the audit activities performed shall be reported half yearly to the board. Serious conditions shall be reported at the first possible board meeting. The biannual reports shall mention completed audits, significant findings, status for follow-up of measures and any overall developments. 2.5 Follow-up and advice Consultancy shall be carried out in a way that safeguards the independence of internal audits. Tenderers shall not take over NTNU ́s management responsibility or decision authority.

title: Czechia – Construction work – Revitalizace sadu Svobody ve Zlíně
description: Předmětem veřejné zakázky je realizace stavebního záměru „Revitalizace sadu Svobody ve Zlíně“, která bude realizována souběžně a v úzké věcné, prostorové a časové vazbě na stavbu „Revitalizace zlínského zámku – I. etapa“. Stavba řeší komplexní obnovu veřejného parku a bezprostředního okolí nemovité kulturní památky Zlínského zámku, a to zejména v rozsahu nových zpevněných a mlatových ploch pro pěší a obslužnou dopravu, veřejného osvětlení, vodních prvků, závlahových systémů, krajinářských a sadových úprav, městského mobiliáře, slaboproudých technologií a souvisejících přeložek a přípojek inženýrských sítí. Stavba je rozdělena na část Park a část Okolí Zlínského zámku, přičemž obě části tvoří jeden funkční a provozní celek a budou realizovány ve vzájemné časové a technologické návaznosti. Součástí předmětu veřejné zakázky jsou rovněž terénní a sadové úpravy včetně následné pětileté péče o výsadbu a terénní úpravy. Plnění předmětu veřejné zakázky bude probíhat za provozu staveniště, sdíleného s dalšími stavebními záměry téhož zadavatele a s činnostmi třetích osob. Součástí plnění je následná péče o výsadbu v trvání 5 let od předání a převzetí stavební části díla Podrobnosti stanoví zadávací dokumentace, zveřejněná na profilu zadavatele
